get.description:
Liveness plus dependency checks. 503 if the database or Redis (the job
queue and the shared rate limiter) can't be reached. Kept for
compatibility (docker-compose uses it); prefer /health/live and
/health/ready.

The process is up and answering. Checks nothing else on purpose: a
platform restarts the container when this fails, and restarting the API
doesn't fix a database outage.

Ready to serve: Postgres and Redis answer, and a worker is alive
(otherwise uploads would never be processed): the Celery worker's
heartbeat, or in inline mode this process's worker task. 503 with the failing part
named otherwise; a load balancer stops sending traffic until it's 200.

delete.description:
Delete your account and everything stored for it: collections,
documents (rows AND files), conversations, usage history and rate-limit
counters. Requires your password. Cannot be undone.

post.description:
Change your password. Every token issued before this (on any device)
stops working; the response carries a fresh one for this client.

Store the file and queue it for processing. 202: accepted, processing
happens in the background; poll GET /documents/{id} for its status.

post.description:
Answer a question from the documents in one of your collections, citing
the sources it used, and save both to a conversation (a new one unless
conversation_id is given). grounded=false means no supplied source backs
the answer (including "I could not find this in your documents").

Like /ask, but streams the answer as server-sent events: meta, then
token events as text is generated, then done (the final answer, with
invalid citations removed: keep this one) or error. See docs/API.md.

Problems found before streaming starts are ordinary HTTP errors: 422 for
the question, 404 for a collection or conversation that isn't yours,
409 if an answer is already being generated in the conversation.

get.description: Your conversations, most recently active first.
A conversation with its messages, oldest first.

Your usage: provider requests and tokens for today and this month, per
kind (from the usage history in Postgres), and your daily quotas (the
live counters the limits enforce). Only ever your own.

ChunkRead.title: ChunkRead
ChunkRead.description:
Output only. owner_id and collection_id are internal bookkeeping (the
caller already knows the document), so they are not exposed.

CitationSnapshot.title: CitationSnapshot
CitationSnapshot.description:
A source as it was when the answer was given. chunk_id may no longer
exist (re-processing a document replaces its chunks); the rest is a copy.

CollectionUpdate.title: CollectionUpdate
CollectionUpdate.description: PATCH input: only fields the client actually sent are changed.

DocumentRead.title: DocumentRead
DocumentRead.description:
Output only. storage_key and owner_id are deliberately not exposed:
clients identify documents by id, never by where bytes live on disk.

SearchResult.title: SearchResult
SearchResult.description:
One matching chunk, with what each search said about it (for
debugging retrieval). distance is the vector (cosine) distance: smaller
= more similar in meaning. Ranks are 1-based; null = not in that list.

UserRead.title: UserRead
UserRead.description: Output. There is deliberately no password field of any kind here.
